title: Larger radius, bigger bit vector
spec: Use Morgan radius 3 with 4096 bits and chirality enabled in the RF.

title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging
spec: In base_preds, replace the single LGBMRegressor with the average of 3 LightGBM models using seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2 (subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3). This lowers GBM variance before stacking. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.

title: Linear-corrected physics baseline
spec: Replace the raw Crippen subtraction with a fitted baseline. Fit Ridge on a small set of descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, FractionCSP3, and the 12 count of ionizable groups from SMARTS) on the training fold only. Use its prediction as the baseline in place of Crippen. The tree models learn the residual, and the baseline is added back. Compute it inside fit_predict so there is no leakage.

title: Kernel ridge on Tanimoto as stack member
spec: Add sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the existing Tanimoto kernel of the Morgan bits as a 4th column in base_preds. It is cheap, and its errors differ from SVR's epsilon-insensitive fit. The meta-learner is the existing positive linear regression.

title: Repeated-seed ExtraTrees with bigger forest
spec: Raise the final ExtraTrees to 1500 trees, with max_features=0.3 and min_samples_leaf=1. Keep 200 trees in the inner stacking folds. This lowers the variance of the main base model at small cost. Also set bootstrap=False explicitly.

title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto as 4th stack member
spec: Add sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) fit on the Tanimoto kernel of the Morgan bits, as a 4th column in base_preds. It reuses the kernel matrix already computed for the SVR, so it costs almost nothing. Change the oof array to 4 columns. Keep the non-negative linear meta-learner.

title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
spec: After featurizing the train set, compute the bit column sums over the Morgan block, and keep only bits set in at least 3 training molecules plus all descriptor columns. Apply the same mask to the test features. Keep the Tanimoto kernel on the original unmasked bits. This reduces noise features for ExtraTrees (max_features=0.3) and speeds the job up.

title: Atom-pair count fingerprint SVR as 4th stack member
spec: Add a fourth base model: SVR with precomputed MinMax kernel (sum of min / sum of max) on atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, count vector). Compute the features inside featurize into a separate array and keep it out of the tree inputs. Add its column to base_preds and the inner OOF array (shape 4 columns) so the positive linear meta-learner weighs it. Use C=5, epsilon=0.1.

title: Add RBF-kernel SVR on scaled descriptors
spec: Add a 4th stack member: SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the RDKit descriptor and group columns. Preprocess them with a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200) fitted on the training fold. This gives the stack a model whose errors differ from the fingerprint models. Use 4 oof columns.

title: Extra stack member: ExtraTrees on descriptors only
spec: Add a fourth base model: ExtraTreesRegressor (300 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2) trained only on the dense columns (descriptors and group counts, no fingerprint bits). The stack then has 4 columns, so oof needs 4 columns and the meta-learner sees them. Its errors should be less correlated with the fingerprint models.

title: Kernel-only larger Morgan for SVR
spec: Compute a separate radius-3, 4096-bit Morgan bit fingerprint, used only for the Tanimoto-SVR kernel. ExtraTrees and LightGBM keep the existing features. Add this block to the cached feature matrix, or compute it in a separate function with a per-SMILES cache. Slice it in base_preds for the SVR.

title: kNN residual neighbor-target feature
spec: Add two dense features to the ExtraTrees and LightGBM inputs: the Tanimoto-weighted mean of the Crippen-residual targets of the 5 most similar training molecules, and the max Tanimoto similarity. For training rows, compute them leave-one-out (exclude self, and ideally exclude same-scaffold neighbors) from the Morgan bit matrix using the existing tanimoto function. For test rows use all training molecules. Append them as columns in base_preds.

title: Test-time augmentation by randomized SMILES atom order
spec: The count of atom-order-dependent features is small, so instead augment the training set: for each training molecule add one extra row whose descriptor features are the same and whose Morgan fingerprint uses a Morgan generator with a different random bit hash. Skip this if it is not meaningful. Simpler alternative: bag ExtraTrees over 3 different max_features values (0.2, 0.3, 0.5) and average them as one stack member. Implement the bagging alternative.

title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto + RF blend
spec: Fit KernelRidge with precomputed MinMax kernel on count fingerprints (alpha 0.5), average with the RF predictions 50/50.

title: Descriptors only LightGBM
spec: Replace the RF with LightGBM (n_estimators 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample_bytree 0.5, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on RDKit 2D descriptors plus Crippen/MolLogP, using nan_to_num and clipping.

title: MAE-fitted meta-learner
spec: Replace the non-negative LinearRegression meta-learner with weights found by minimizing mean absolute error of the out-of-fold stacked predictions. Use scipy.optimize.minimize (Powell or SLSQP) over 3 weights with bounds [0,1] and a sum-to-1 normalization, starting from equal weights. This matches the MAE loss.

title: MAE-fitted meta-learner
spec: Replace LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner with weights found by minimizing mean absolute error of oof @ w over the simplex-like constraint w>=0 using scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP, start at equal weights 1/3, bounds (0,2)), no intercept. The loss is MAE so the blend should be fit for MAE directly.

title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto base model
spec: Add KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the Morgan Tanimoto kernel as an extra stack column (on the Crippen residual). It is cheap, and its smooth predictions differ from those of SVR. Update the OOF array to 4 columns.

title: Linear-corrected Crippen baseline
spec: Replace the plain Crippen residual with a fitted baseline. Fit a Ridge regression (alpha 1) on the training set using [Crippen logP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD count, HBA count, fraction of sp3 carbons, and the 8 ionizable-group counts], standardized. Use the out-of-fold ridge prediction as the baseline, so the residual targets aren't leaked. Fit the final ridge on all training data for the test baseline. The trees, LightGBM and SVR then fit y minus this baseline. Add the baseline back at the end.

title: Sample weights by scaffold rarity
spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Give each molecule the weight 1/sqrt(scaffold count). Pass the weights as sample_weight to ExtraTrees, LightGBM and SVR (SVR.fit takes sample_weight with a precomputed kernel). This counters overrepresented scaffolds, which fits the scaffold-split evaluation.

title: Gaussian-process-style kNN residual stage
spec: After the stack prediction, compute the OOF stack residuals on training molecules, then for each test molecule add 0.5 * Tanimoto-weighted mean (weights = sim^3, top 5 neighbours with sim>0.5) of the neighbours' OOF residuals; if no neighbours exceed 0.5, add nothing. Use the OOF predictions from the existing inner loop and the meta weights.

title: Quantile-transformed target
spec: Train base models on a monotone-transformed Crippen residual: r = y - crippen; fit a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') on training r (scaled by the training std back to original units), fit stack on transformed values, and invert the transform on the meta predictions before adding Crippen. Uses sklearn only.

title: Scaffold-grouped inner stacking folds
spec: In fit_predict, replace the random inner KFold used to build the out-of-fold stack predictions with GroupKFold, grouped by Murcko scaffold (generic scaffold string mapped to integer ids). This makes the OOF predictions mimic the unseen-scaffold evaluation, so the meta weights are better calibrated. Nothing else changes.

title: Drop rare and constant fingerprint bits
spec: After featurizing, compute the column sums of the Morgan bit block on the training matrix. Keep only bits set in at least 5 training molecules, and always keep the descriptor and group columns. Apply the same column mask to the test matrix. The mask applies to the ExtraTrees and LightGBM inputs. The SVR kernel can use the masked bits too. This reduces noise features and speeds up the fits.

title: Meta-learner trained with MAE
spec: Replace the LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative weight vector found by scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP). Minimize the mean absolute error of oof @ w against y, with w >= 0 and sum(w) = 1, starting from equal weights. Predict with base_preds @ w. This matches the MAE loss and resists outliers.

title: Larger-radius Morgan hashed to 4096 bits for the kernel only
spec: Keep the tree features as they are. For the SVR Tanimoto kernel, build separate binary Morgan fingerprints with radius 3 and 4096 bits, stored in a separate array. Compute the kernel on these instead of the first N_BITS columns. Everything else stays the same.

title: Linear-corrected Crippen baseline
spec: Instead of subtracting raw MolLogP, fit a Ridge (alpha 1) on the training fold using [MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, fraction of carboxylic acids and basic amines from GROUPS counts] to predict y, and use its prediction as baseline for residuals (trained on the full training set; in the inner OOF loop reuse the same baseline for simplicity). Add the baseline back at predict time.

title: Second-stage residual correction with kNN
spec: After the stacked prediction, compute out-of-fold stack residuals on the training set from the inner CV. For each test molecule, take the Tanimoto-weighted mean (sim^3, top 5 neighbours with sim>0.6) of the neighbours' OOF residuals. Add 0.5 times it to the prediction. Do nothing when no neighbours qualify.

title: Per-model feature subsetting: SVR on Morgan+groups kernel mix
spec: Change the SVR kernel to the average of the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits and an RBF kernel on standardized RDKit descriptors (QuantileTransformer-normal scaled, gamma=1/n_features). Keep precomputed SVR with C=5. This gives the third stack member descriptor information while keeping it distinct from the trees.

title: Deeper LightGBM with dart and strong regularization
spec: Change the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart', n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15, drop_rate=0.1, colsample_bytree=0.2, reg_lambda=5, min_child_samples=15. Keeps the other members unchanged; aims for a more diverse, better-regularized boosting member.

title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging inside stack
spec: In base_preds, replace the single LightGBM with the average of 3 LightGBM models using different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.3. Keep it as one stack column. This reduces variance of the boosted model.

title: Residual-corrected second-stage on stack error
spec: After the meta-learner prediction, fit a small LightGBM (100 trees, depth 3, lr 0.05) on the out-of-fold stacked residual (y minus the meta prediction on OOF) using only 20 key dense features (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, the 8 group counts, and so on). Add its prediction, scaled by 0.5, to the final output. This tries to correct systematic ionization and polarity errors.

title: Atom-pair/torsion counts plus cached features combined
spec: Memoize per-SMILES features in a module-level dict so each molecule is featurized once. Append 1024-bit atom-pair and 1024-bit topological-torsion count fingerprints (log1p-transformed) to the feature matrix used by ExtraTrees and LightGBM only. The SVR keeps using the first N_BITS Morgan columns. Keep the rest of the stack unchanged.
